definition: Convivial means characterized by feasting, drinking, and a merry, friendly social atmosphere.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word convivial. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know convivial should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The graduation dinner was a convivial affair, with heaping plates, clinking glasses, and laughter that carried into the street.
A cheerful gathering simply has a light, happy mood, while a convivial one adds shared food, drink, and toasts to the merriment.
A convivial banquet is festive but still warm and sociable, while an uproarious one tips over into wild noise and near-chaos.

Festive means cheerful and celebratory, and it is tied to an occasion - holidays, victories, decorations. A hallway strung with lights is festive with no one in it. Convivial cannot happen without people: it needs merry company sharing food and drink. An empty banquet hall can look festive; only the feast itself is convivial.

Merry means full of lively cheerfulness, and it describes the feeling itself wherever it appears - a merry laugh, a merry mood, one merry child. Convivial names a whole social scene: people gathered over food and drink, enjoying one another. A single hiker can be merry alone on a trail; it takes a table of companions to be convivial.

Every autumn, the whole block gathers in the Riveras' backyard for the harvest potluck.
Tables sag under trays of tamales, casseroles, and pies, someone always brings a guitar, and neighbors linger over cups of hot cider trading stories until the porch lights come on.
Even newcomers are pulled into the toasts and the laughter within minutes.
By dessert, the convivial mood has turned a yard full of strangers and acquaintances into something like a family reunion.
The gathering's festive atmosphere of shared food, drink, and merry company is exactly what convivial describes.

Convivial describes the festive mood of an event or gathering built around shared food and drink (a convivial dinner party, a convivial reception, a convivial atmosphere).
Use it for the spirit of the occasion itself rather than for one person's everyday personality.

For eight months of the year, the research station at Halvorsen Ridge is cut off by ice, and its twelve crew members see no other human faces.
Visitors expect the isolation to breed silence; instead they find the galley loud on Friday nights, when the cook lays out a long table of bread, stew, and canned peaches.
The station manager calls these dinners the most convivial hours of the winter, and she schedules them as deliberately as fuel checks.
Crews that eat together, she argues, forgive one another faster; laughter over a shared pot does what no conflict workshop can.
Psychologists who study remote outposts agree: the feast matters less than the fellowship it creates, and both matter more than the menu.
